title: Azure Functions lab deployment fails because storage setting is missing
failure_log: Function host started but HTTP trigger did not become available
Error: AzureWebJobsStorage is missing or empty
Host initialization failed because storage connection could not be resolved
expected_outcome: HTTP trigger responds successfully after deployment
observed_outcome: Function app deploys but runtime host cannot start the trigger
recovery_summary: Recovery plan targets the confirmed lab failure: Missing AzureWebJobsStorage application setting
fix_steps: Confirm the Function App belongs to the synthetic lab scenario.
Inspect current application settings before changing configuration.
Add or repair the AzureWebJobsStorage setting using synthetic lab storage values only.
Restart the Function App after the setting is corrected.
rollback_steps: Record the previous app setting value before applying changes.
Restore the previous value if the host still fails to start.
Restart the Function App again after rollback.
verification_steps: Confirm the function host starts without storage configuration errors.
Confirm the HTTP trigger endpoint responds.
Confirm deployment logs no longer mention missing AzureWebJobsStorage.

assessment_questions.question: What setting is commonly required for an Azure Functions host to start storage-backed runtime services?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: AzureWebJobsStorage must be present and valid for the synthetic lab Function App.

assessment_questions.question: What should the learner verify after repairing the Function App setting?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: The host starts without storage errors and the HTTP trigger responds.

assessment_questions.question: Why should connection strings not be printed or committed during recovery?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: They are secrets and must not appear in logs or source control.

manager_risk_areas: Application setting verification before code changes
Rollback discipline after failed recovery attempts
Grounded explanation of root cause and verification evidence
safety_notes: Do not expose real connection strings
Use placeholder-free environment examples in documentation

title: Azure DevOps release lab stalls because environment approval is missing
failure_log: Release pipeline created a deployment job
Deployment remained pending before production stage
Error: environment approval required before deployment can continue
expected_outcome: Pipeline deploys only after required approval is reviewed and granted
observed_outcome: Pipeline build succeeds but deployment never reaches the target environment
known_root_cause: Missing required environment approval for gated deployment
recovery_summary: Recovery plan targets the confirmed lab failure: missing required environment approval for gated deployment
fix_steps: Confirm the pipeline and environment belong to the intended synthetic lab.
Inspect the environment approval and check configuration before editing the pipeline.
Add or request the required synthetic approver for the target environment.
Re-run or resume the deployment after approval is granted.
rollback_steps: Record the previous approval configuration before changing it.
Restore the previous gate configuration if the deployment behaves unexpectedly.
Cancel the pending synthetic deployment if approval settings remain incorrect.
verification_steps: Confirm the release waits at the approval gate.
Confirm approval allows the deployment to continue.
Confirm deployment logs show the gated stage completed successfully.

assessment_questions.question: Why can a CI/CD pipeline build succeed while deployment remains blocked?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: A required environment approval or gate can pause deployment even after the build succeeds.

assessment_questions.question: What should be recorded before changing deployment approval settings?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: The previous approval or gate configuration should be recorded for rollback.

assessment_questions.question: What is the safest verification after an approval-gated deployment is repaired?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: Confirm the pipeline waits for approval, resumes after approval, and completes the gated stage successfully.

safety_notes: Do not expose real environment names
Do not bypass real production approvals

title: Azure VM lab fails because inbound NSG rule blocks connectivity
lab_name: VM connectivity and network security lab
failure_log: Connection test to management port failed
Network security group does not allow required inbound traffic
expected_outcome: Learner connects to the VM through the approved synthetic management path
observed_outcome: VM is running but the learner cannot connect through the expected management path
known_root_cause: Missing inbound NSG rule for the approved synthetic management path
recovery_summary: Recovery plan targets the confirmed lab failure: missing inbound NSG rule for the approved synthetic management path
fix_steps: Confirm the VM and network security group belong to the intended synthetic lab.
Inspect the effective security rules before changing network configuration.
Add or repair the inbound NSG rule for the approved synthetic management path.
Retry connectivity after the rule is applied.
rollback_steps: Record the previous NSG rule set before applying changes.
Remove the new inbound rule if verification fails or the rule is too broad.
Restore the previous NSG rule configuration after rollback.
verification_steps: Confirm effective security rules include the expected inbound allow rule.
Confirm connectivity succeeds through the approved synthetic management path.
Confirm no broader-than-required inbound exposure was introduced.

assessment_questions.question: Why can a VM be running while connection attempts still fail?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: Network security rules can block required inbound traffic even when the VM itself is healthy.

assessment_questions.question: What should be checked before editing an NSG rule?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: The learner should inspect effective security rules and confirm the target resource is the intended synthetic lab resource.

assessment_questions.question: What is a safe verification after adding an inbound NSG rule?
assessment_questions.expected_answer: Confirm connectivity succeeds and no broader-than-required inbound exposure was introduced.

safety_notes: Use synthetic IP and management paths only
Do not expose real public IP addresses
Do not recommend broad inbound access
